I'm planning to add a new training + experience system to the Polyglot agent platform. I need to understand the EXISTING training and memory infrastructure before designing it.

Working directory: /Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Polyglot

Focus areas:
1. /Users/yashbaldha/.claude/memory/ — full directory tree, what's inside
2. /Users/yashbaldha/.claude/agents/tutor.md — the Tutor agent definition (agent trainer)
3. /Users/yashbaldha/.claude/agents/mira.md — Mira memory & training agent
4. /Users/yashbaldha/.claude/agents/forge.md — agent architect (creates new agents)
5. /Users/yashbaldha/.claude/commands/train.md — the /train slash command
6. Polyglot project files related to agent performance, run history, training: run-history.json, agent-runs.json, memory-audit-log.json
7. Polyglot/src/server.js — any routes dealing with training, memory, agent performance

Questions to answer:

A) **How does Tutor currently work?** — read tutor.md and summarize its actual instructions. What does it train, how often, what inputs does it use?

B) **How does Mira currently capture lessons?** — same for mira.md. What's the output format for a training session?

C) **Memory brain structure** — give me the full tree of ~/.claude/memory/. Identify:
   - patterns/good/ and patterns/avoid/ — do these have per-agent subfolders or are they shared?
   - projects/ — per-project lessons
   - user/feedback.md — corrections
   - Any "experience" or "skill level" or "years" concept? (Probably none, but check)

D) **Agent run tracking** — what does run-history.json / agent-runs.json look like? Do we track per-agent:
   - Number of runs
   - Success/failure rate  
   - Duration
   - Which anti-patterns were triggered
   - Which lessons were learned
   Give me the data shape.

E) **How training results get persisted back to agents** — when Tutor/Mira learn something, does it get written into the agent's own .md file? Into memory/? Both? Show me the actual flow.

F) **The /train command** — what does it do step by step.

Report format: sections A–F, under 500 words. Include specific file paths. Quote key snippets only when showing data shape.

7	---
8	
9	# 🎓 Tutor — Agent Trainer
10	
11	You are **Tutor**. Every week you make all 32 agents smarter. You don't design new agents (Forge does) and you don't compress them (Refactor does) — you inject fresh knowledge and patch weaknesses.
12	
13	---
14	
15	## MANDATORY MEMORY LOADS
16	
17	- `~/.claude/memory/MEMORY.md`
18	- `~/.claude/memory/patterns/good/production-agent-mindset.md`
19	- `~/.claude/memory/patterns/good/universal-auto-fix-loop.md`
20	- `~/.claude/memory/patterns/good/universal-smart-defaults.md`
21	- `~/.claude/memory/user/feedback.md` (highest priority training signal)
22	- `~/.claude/memory/agent-registry.json`
23	- Latest Trend report: `~/.claude/memory/intelligence/trends/latest.md`
24	- Latest Mira learnings: `~/.claude/memory/learnings/latest.md`
25	
26	---
27	
28	## Core Responsibility
29	
30	Every Sunday at 02:00 UTC, run a training cycle that:
31	1. Ingests all training signal from the last 7 days (feedback, Trend, Mira, gap report).
32	2. Maps each signal to the agent(s) it should update.
33	3. Produces a training delta per agent: new anti-patterns, updated smart defaults, new failure modes to auto-fix, refreshed domain knowledge.
34	4. Applies deltas to agent .md files via surgical Edit calls.
35	5. Emits a training report to `~/.claude/memory/agent-evolution/training-YYYY-WW.md`.
36	6. Triggers Refactor if any agent exceeds 4000 tokens after update.
37	
38	---
39	
40	## Training Signal Sources (priority order)
41	
42	| Priority | Source | Weight | Notes |
43	|---|---|---|---|
44	| P0 | `user/feedback.md` | highest | Yash corrections override everything |
45	| P1 | Verdict post-decision monitoring | high | Real-world outcomes of agent decisions |
46	| P2 | Mira learnings | high | Extracted patterns from completed work |
47	| P3 | Trend synthesis report | medium | Market-driven new patterns |
48	| P4 | Gap report (from Forge) | medium | Structural weaknesses |
49	| P5 | Community wisdom (Skool/Reddit via Harvest→Prism→Trend) | low | Validated external signal |
50	
51	---
52	
53	## Training Delta Format
54	
55	For each agent updated, emit:
56	
57	```yaml
58	agent: koda
59	week: 2026-W15
60	deltas:
61	  - type: anti-pattern
62	    content: "Never use useEffect for server data fetching — always use TanStack Query"
63	    source: "P0 - user/feedback.md 2026-04-09"
64	    section: anti-patterns
65	  - type: smart-default
66	    content: "When no auth library specified, default to @supabase/ssr for Next.js projects"
67	    source: "P2 - mira learnings"
68	    section: smart-defaults
69	  - type: auto-fix
70	    content: "If TS build fails with TS2307 on path alias, verify tsconfig paths match vite.config alias"
71	    source: "P1 - verdict monitoring"
72	    section: auto-fix-loop
73	```
74	
75	---
76	
77	## Auto-Fix Loop
78	
79	**MANDATORY: Load `~/.claude/memory/patterns/good/universal-auto-fix-loop.md` before every task.**
80	**MANDATORY: Load `~/.claude/memory/patterns/good/universal-smart-defaults.md` for autonomous defaults.**
81	
82	| Attempt | Failure | Fix |
83	|---|---|---|
84	| 1 | Edit call fails (string not unique) | Re-read target section, add more context, retry |
85	| 2 | Markdown fence integrity broken | Count fences, patch the mismatch, validate, retry |
86	| 3 | Agent file > 4000 tokens post-edit | Dispatch Refactor, wait, resume |
87	| 4 | Conflicting signals (P0 vs P3) | P0 always wins, log conflict to changelog |
88	| 5 | Registry version hash mismatch | Reload, reapply, retry once, then fail loud |
89	
90	---
91	
92	## Smart Defaults
93	
94	- **No training signal this week** → Emit "no-op cycle" report, skip edits.
95	- **Agent file missing** → Log to Forge as gap, skip.
96	- **Delta would duplicate existing anti-pattern** → Skip, log as "already learned".
97	- **Signal mentions an agent not in registry** → Dispatch Forge to investigate.
98	- **Yash feedback contradicts existing pattern** → Yash always wins, archive old pattern to `~/.claude/memory/patterns/archived/`.
99	
100	---
101	
102	## Weekly Cycle
103	
104	```
105	Sunday 02:00 UTC
106	  ├─ Pull all training signals (7d window)
107	  ├─ Map signals → agents
108	  ├─ Generate deltas per agent
109	  ├─ Apply deltas via Edit (surgical, never rewrite)
110	  ├─ Verify fence integrity
111	  ├─ Check token counts
112	  ├─ Update registry version hashes
113	  ├─ Emit training-YYYY-WW.md report
114	  ├─ Dispatch Refactor if needed
115	  └─ Send digest to Yash
116	```
117	
118	---
119	
120	## Completion Proof
121	
122	Training cycle is done when:
123	1. ✅ Report exists at `~/.claude/memory/agent-evolution/training-YYYY-WW.md`
124	2. ✅ Every applied delta has a source citation
125	3. ✅ Every edited agent file has even code fence count
126	4. ✅ No agent file exceeds 4000 tokens (or Refactor is dispatched)
127	5. ✅ Registry version hashes bumped for every edited agent
128	6. ✅ P0 (Yash feedback) signals are all consumed — none left in queue
129	7. ✅ Conflict log entries resolved or escalated to Yash
130	8. ✅ Weekly digest sent
131	
132	---
133	
134	## Anti-Patterns
135	
136	1. ❌ **Rewriting entire agent files** — always surgical Edit, never full rewrite.
137	2. ❌ **Ignoring Yash feedback** — P0 is non-negotiable, consume every item.
138	3. ❌ **Applying deltas without source citation** — every change must be traceable.
139	4. ❌ **Adding deltas without validating fence integrity** — breaks all agents downstream.
140	5. ❌ **Letting agent files grow past 4000 tokens silently** — always dispatch Refactor.
141	6. ❌ **Training agents based on single data points** — require ≥2 signals for P3-P5.
142	7. ❌ **Skipping the registry version bump** — breaks Mira's change tracking.
143	8. ❌ **Running without loading Trend's latest report** — stale signal = stale training.
144	9. ❌ **Applying contradictory deltas in the same cycle** — resolve conflicts before edit.
145	10. ❌ **Forgetting to archive superseded patterns** — memory pollution compounds.
146	
147	---
148	
149	## Handoff
150	
151	- **Upstream:** Harvest → Prism → Trend (fresh market signal), Mira (learnings), Verdict (outcomes), Yash (feedback)
152	- **Downstream:** Refactor (if token bloat), Mira (changelog sync), all 32 agents (updated)
153	- **Partner:** Forge (new agent design), Refactor (compression)
154	- **Monitored by:** Hawk
155	
156	You are the compound interest of the factory. One delta a week, 52 weeks a year, 32 agents × years = every agent is a genius by year two.

90	- Agent produced code that didn't compile

92	- Objective was abandoned or partially completed

102	**Input Validation:** ✅ / ⚠️ / ❌
103	**Issues Found:** [any concerning patterns]
104	**Artifacts Quality:** [assessment]
105	**Proceed with Training:** yes/no
106	```

108	### Step 1B: Functional Verification Audit
109	
110	Before extracting lessons, Mira MUST verify the agents' claims about what was built:
111	
112	**Verify the app actually works:**
113	```bash
114	# 1. Does the app build?
115	npm run build
116	# If fails: log "Build broken — agents claimed done but build fails"
117	
118	# 2. Does the app start?
119	npm start &
120	sleep 5
121	curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://localhost:3000/
122	# If not 200: log "App doesn't start — agents claimed done but server fails"
123	
124	# 3. Do claimed pages load with real content?
125	for route in "/" "/login" "/dashboard" "/pricing" "/admin" "/settings"; do
126	  SIZE=$(curl -s http://localhost:3000$route | wc -c)
127	  echo "$route: $SIZE bytes"
128	  if [ "$SIZE" -lt 500 ]; then
129	    echo "⚠️ $route appears EMPTY — agent claimed this was built"
130	  fi
131	done
132	
133	# 4. Is there stub/placeholder content?
134	curl -s http://localhost:3000/ | grep -i "coming soon\|todo\|placeholder\|lorem ipsum\|not implemented"
135	# If matches: log "Stub content in production pages"
136	```

140	- Agent said "billing integrated" but pricing page shows $0 or placeholder prices
141	- Agent said "admin panel built" but /admin returns 404
142	- Agent said "auth working" but login form doesn't submit
143	- Agent said "dashboard ready" but it shows only empty states with no data fetching
144	- Build succeeds but app has no functional features

Perfect! Now I have comprehensive understanding. Let me compile the final report.

---

## EXISTING TRAINING & MEMORY INFRASTRUCTURE REPORT

### A) Tutor Agent — Current Training System

**File:** `/Users/yashbaldha/.claude/agents/tutor.md` (6,461 bytes)

**How it works:** Weekly (Sundays 02:00 UTC), Tutor runs a 7-day training cycle that injects new knowledge into all 25+ agents. It ingests 5 priority signal sources (user feedback > verdict monitoring > Mira learnings > Trend reports > gaps), generates per-agent training deltas (anti-patterns, smart defaults, auto-fix rules), and applies them via surgical Edit calls to agent .md files. Every delta is source-cited and fenced correctly.

**Training delta format:** YAML blocks with type (anti-pattern|smart-default|auto-fix), content, source, section. Example:
```yaml
- type: anti-pattern
  content: "Never use useEffect for server data fetching — always use TanStack Query"
  source: "P0 - user/feedback.md 2026-04-09"
```

**Key constraint:** Never rewrite full agent files, only surgical edits. Agent files must stay <4000 tokens or Refactor is dispatched. Training is non-negotiable — P0 (Yash feedback) always wins.

---

### B) Mira Agent — Lesson Extraction System

**File:** `/Users/yashbaldha/.claude/agents/mira.md` (71,967 bytes)

**How it captures lessons:** Mira runs after every build session. It:
1. **Validates work** — checks that agent output actually works (build succeeds, app starts, pages load)
2. **Reviews session** — extracts what was built, errors encountered, decisions made
3. **Classifies learnings** — sorts into: good patterns, antipatterns, agent reliability, stack knowledge, project decisions, user feedback
4. **Writes to memory** — updates `~/.claude/memory/patterns/good/[category].md`, `patterns/avoid/antipatterns.md`, `stacks/[stack-name].md`, `user/feedback.md`, `decisions/[date]-decision.md`

**Training session output format:**
```markdown
### [Title]
**Context:** [Stack, feature type]
**Pattern:** [Exactly what to do or avoid]
**Why:** [Why it matters]
**Relationships:** [Cross-references]
**Example:** [Code if needed]
**Source:** [Project, date]
**Usage Metric:** 0 (initially)
**Knowledge Version:** v1
```

**Bug tracking:** Append-only JSONL file at `~/.claude/memory/lessons/bugs.jsonl` with schema containing: id, date, project, stack, agent_that_shipped, severity (P1-P4), category, symptom, root_cause, detection_method, time_to_detect, time_to_fix, lesson, antipattern_tag.

---

### C) Memory Brain Structure — Full Directory Tree

**Path:** `/Users/yashbaldha/.claude/memory/`

**Structure (NOT per-agent):**
- `patterns/good/` — 40+ shared pattern files (auth-patterns.md, billing-patterns.md, autonomous-agent-protocol.md, production-validated-patterns.md, etc.)
- `patterns/avoid/` — shared antipatterns.md + _archive/
- `stacks/` — technology stacks (saas-nextjs-supabase-railway.md, shopify/, ai-patterns.md)
- `projects/` — per-project decision logs
- `user/` — feedback.md (highest-priority corrections from Yash), profile.md, decision-simulator.md
- `design/` — UI/UX patterns, design tokens, standards
- `content/` — copy patterns, brand voice
- `decisions/` — major architectural decisions with reasoning
- `lessons/` — bugs.jsonl (source of truth), agents/ (per-agent lesson files), patterns-emerged.md (weekly synthesis)
- `intake/` — session validation logs

**No per-agent subdirs in patterns/good/ or patterns/avoid/** — all patterns are shared globally. Individual agents get trained by Tutor injecting deltas into their own .md files.

**No "experience" or "years" concept yet** — only: usage_metric (retrieval count), knowledge_version (v1, v2...), firstSeen / lastSeen timestamps on agent profiles.

---

### D) Agent Run Tracking — Data Shape

**File:** `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Polyglot/agent-runs.json`

**Per-agent run record (agent_runs.json):**
```json
{
  "id": "mnrycwfvvuk6q",
  "agentName": "scout",
  "prompt": "...(truncated to 200 chars)",
  "source": "project-chat|direct|scheduled|orchestration",
  "timestamp": "2026-04-09T20:51:39.451Z",
  "duration": 112251,              // milliseconds
  "status": "success|failed",
  "promptChars": 68,
  "outputChars": 1181,
  "estimatedTokens": 313,
  "estimatedCost": 0.004491,
  "error": null,
  "metadata": { projectId, conversationId }
}
```

**Agent learning profile (agent-learning.json, in-memory structure):**
```json
{
  "agents": {
    "scout": {
      "totalRuns": N,
      "successRuns": N,
      "failedRuns": N,
      "avgDuration": 112.3,
      "avgTokens": 450.2,
      "avgCost": 0.00567,
      "streak": 5,
      "bestStreak": 12,
      "firstSeen": "2026-03-15T...",
      "lastSeen": "2026-04-11T...",
      "taskTypes": {
        "general": { "runs": 45, "successes": 42, "avgDuration": 110 },
        "code-generation": { "runs": 28, "successes": 27, "avgDuration": 125 }
      }
    }
  },
  "taskTypes": {
    "code-generation": {
      "bestAgent": "koda",

      "agents": {
        "koda": { "successRate": 96, "avgDuration": 115, "runs": 50 },
        "nova": { "successRate": 88, "avgDuration": 120, "runs": 40 }
      }
    }
  },
  "updatedAt": "2026-04-11T13:21:00Z"
}
```

**Metrics tracked per agent:**
- Total runs, success/failure counts, success rate
- Avg duration (exponential moving average, alpha=0.1)
- Avg tokens & cost (same EMA)
- Streak (current & best)
- Per-task-type breakdown (which tasks it's best at)

---

### E) Training Results Flow — How Learning Gets Persisted Back

**Cycle:**

1. **Agent runs** → `logAgentRun()` called, creates entry in `agent-runs.json`
2. **Auto-learn trigger** → `recordLearning(agentName, taskType, outcome)` called automatically
3. **Update learning DB** → agent-learning.json profile updated with EMA stats, streak, task-type breakdown
4. **Weekly Tutor run** (Sunday 02:00 UTC):
   - Reads all training signals (user/feedback.md, Mira learnings, Trend reports, agent-learning.json stats)
   - Generates deltas per agent
   - **Applies to agent .md directly** via Edit calls (adds sections to YAML frontmatter or appends to body)
   - Persists both to agent's file AND to `~/.claude/memory/agent-evolution/training-YYYY-WW.md` report

5. **Training bake endpoint** (`POST /api/training/:name/bake`):
   - Reads stored corrections from `~/.claude/training/{agentName}.json`
   - Appends them to agent .md as "Baked Training Corrections" section
   - Archives corrections to `.archived.json`

**Flow diagram:**
```
Run → agent-runs.json → recordLearning() → agent-learning.json (stats)
                                  ↓
                     User feedback in ~/.claude/memory/user/feedback.md
                                  ↓
                     Tutor (Sunday) reads all signals
                                  ↓
                     Generates deltas (YAML format)
                                  ↓
                     Surgical Edit → agent.md updated
                                  ↓
                     Report to ~/.claude/memory/agent-evolution/training-YYYY-WW.md
```

---

### F) The `/train` Command — Step-by-Step

**File:** `/Users/yashbaldha/.claude/commands/train.md`

**Command execution:**
1. User runs `/train` after completing a feature, fixing a bug, or making a major decision
2. Mira (trainer agent) loads:
   - All session artifacts (agent outputs, code diffs, decisions)
   - Reference files: production-agent-mindset.md, autonomous-agent-protocol.md, production-validated-patterns.md
3. Mira performs input validation:
   - What was the objective? (feature/fix/decision)
   - Did agents produce complete output?
   - Did the build succeed?
   - Any red flags (placeholder content, reverted changes)?
4. Mira reviews work:
   - What was built/fixed/decided?
   - What errors were encountered and how resolved?
   - Which patterns were reused?
   - What took longer than expected?
5. Mira classifies learnings into 11 categories (good pattern, antipattern, agent reliability, stack knowledge, project decision, user feedback, copy pattern, AI pattern, etc.)
6. Mira writes/updates memory files in appropriate locations
7. Updates MEMORY.md index if new files created

**No explicit per-agent experience tracking yet** — the /train command focuses on extracting generalizable lessons, not profiling individual agent skill.

---

## Summary for Your Design

**GAPS to fill with a new training + experience system:**
1. Agent **experience points/levels** — no concept of "years building React" or "skill in billing integrations"
2. Per-agent **specialty tracking** — which agents are best at which domains (only task-type breakdown exists in agent-learning.json)
3. **Explicit curriculum** — agents aren't currently routed to specific training topics based on weakness
4. **Knowledge decay detection** — patterns >6 months old aren't flagged as stale in memory
5. **Anti-pattern frequency** — we don't track "this agent hits this antipattern 3x per week, needs focused training"

**Existing infrastructure you can build on:**
- `agent-learning.json` structure (add experience_points, specialties, weak_areas fields)
- `lessons/bugs.jsonl` schema (already extensible with agent_skill_gap field)
- Tutor's weekly cycle (can trigger per-agent focused training based on weakness scores)
- Memory files already support versioning (Knowledge Version: v1, v2...)
